artist.name: Rikith Reddy
artist.bio: I'm Rikith Reddy — a data scientist by day and a watercolour artist by conviction. Painting is where I process the world: the stillness of a bird on a branch, the chaos of water over rock, the sacred geometry of mythology. Every piece starts with observation and ends somewhere I didn't expect. I work primarily in Daniel Smith watercolours on Brusto 300GSM cold pressed paper, often layering ink linework and masking techniques to push the medium into new territory.

landscape.name: Landscapes
landscape.description: Waterfalls, mountains, and natural vistas painted with expressive wet-on-wet washes

birds.name: Birds
birds.description: Intimate studies of birds — each one a meditation on colour, feather, and stillness

mixed-media.name: Mixed Media
mixed-media.description: Watercolour combined with ink linework, scratching, and geometric overlays

mythology.name: Mythology
mythology.description: Depictions of Hindu deities and spiritual subjects, rendered in vivid pigment

superb-fairy-wren.name: Superb Fairy-wren
superb-fairy-wren.description: A series of paintings exploring the superb fairy-wren in different styles — from classical observation to mixed-media experiments.

waterfalls.name: Waterfalls
waterfalls.description: A collection of waterfall studies painted across different locations and moods.

paintings.title: Forest Cascade
paintings.description: A cascading waterfall framed by lush green forest canopy. Light filters through the trees, catching the cool blue-white rush of water as it tumbles over warm rocky ledges into a still pool below.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet washes for foliage, dry brush for rock textures, lifted highlights for waterfall spray

paintings.title: Coastal Ridgeline
paintings.description: A dramatic mountain ridgeline plunges to meet a coastal inlet, its slopes vivid with lime-green moss against dark volcanic rock. Storm clouds gather overhead, parting just enough to let a pale light catch the still water.
paintings.technique: Bold wet-on-wet sky washes, negative painting for mountain silhouettes

paintings.title: European Robin
paintings.description: A European robin confronts the viewer head-on, its orange-red breast glowing against a dark tangle of branches. White ink linework radiates outward in dense hatch marks — part scientific illustration, part controlled chaos.
paintings.technique: Watercolour base, white gel pen and ink linework overlay, masking fluid for highlights

paintings.title: Superb Fairy-wren I
paintings.description: A male superb fairy-wren perches on a bare twig against a soft textured grey background. The iridescent cobalt blue of his crown and cheeks is rendered in layers of Phthalo Blue and French Ultramarine, the granulation of the background paper left visible.
paintings.technique: Controlled wet-on-dry layering, granulation effects in background wash

paintings.title: Superb Fairy-wren II
paintings.description: A superb fairy-wren stands alert on a weathered post, facing left. The granulated violet-grey background has a crystalline frost-like quality, while the bird's blue crown anchors the composition with vivid colour.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet background with salt texture, detailed dry-brush feather work

paintings.title: Summit Lines
paintings.description: A snow-dusted mountain peak rendered in deep Phthalo Blue and Hansa Yellow, overlaid with topographic contour lines in white ink. The result sits somewhere between landscape painting and cartographic diagram.
paintings.technique: Watercolour base, white ink contour line overlay, wax resist for snow highlights

paintings.title: Superb Fairy-wren III
paintings.description: A superb fairy-wren stands on dark ground, surrounded by radiating white lines and geometric dot patterns — like a signal emanating from the bird's small, electric body. The dark background makes the cobalt crown blaze.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, white gel pen geometric overlay, masking fluid highlights

paintings.title: Above the Cloud Line
paintings.description: A high-altitude peak rises above a sea of cloud, its snow fields catching the first pink light of dawn. The sky burns in bands of rose, gold, and cerulean — the kind of light that exists for about four minutes and then is gone.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet gradients, granulation medium in clouds, lifted highlights on snow

paintings.title: Red-crowned Cranes
paintings.description: Two red-crowned cranes wade in golden-hour water, their grey and white plumage glowing against the warm orange reflections. A yellow sun hangs behind a tree line of dark brushstrokes — simple, direct, joyful.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet washes, minimal linework for bird detail

paintings.title: Veiled Falls
paintings.description: A wide waterfall drops into dark void, flanked by silhouetted trees and birds cutting across a pale sky. Green and yellow canopy presses in from all sides, dappled and alive.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet canopy washes, dry brush waterfall, negative painting for birds

paintings.title: Spectral Owl
paintings.description: A young owl rendered in full spectral colour — blues, pinks, yellows, greens bleeding and blooming across its feathers. The watercolour is pushed to the edge of abstraction while the form stays intact. Pure joy in pigment.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet colour blooms, salt texture on background, controlled lifting

paintings.title: Rock Pool
paintings.description: A forest stream breaks over flat stones into a quiet pool below. Trees frame the scene from above, their canopy letting in shafts of pale light that catch the foam. Dark rocks anchor the foreground.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet foliage, dry brush for rock texture, lifted highlights for water flow

paintings.title: Sun Conure
paintings.description: A sun conure perches on a branch against a deep emerald background, its plumage a riot of orange, yellow, and green. White ink lines radiate outward like light from a source, and star-like dots scatter through the darkness around it.
paintings.technique: Deep wet-on-wet background, detailed feather layering, white gel pen starburst overlay

paintings.title: Fairy-wren in the Vortex
paintings.description: A fairy-wren stands against a swirling white vortex, electric blue splatter marks scattered around it like sparks. The composition is dramatic — a small creature at the centre of its own storm.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour ground, wet-on-wet swirl blending, blue ink splatter, masking fluid highlights

paintings.title: Ganesha
paintings.description: Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles, rendered in a deep crimson and violet palette with grey-white form. His hands meet in namaste, a tilak on his forehead, a jewelled crown above. Painted with reverence and precision.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet background with dark tones, controlled layering for the figure, white ink detail work

paintings.title: Blue Flycatcher
paintings.description: A Tickell's blue flycatcher clings to a slender branch, its cobalt-blue head and back contrasting sharply with the warm rufous-orange of its breast. The background is a soft wash of muted grey-green, letting the bird's jewel-like colours do all the talking.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-dry layering for bird detail, loose wet-on-wet background wash

paintings.title: Alpine Dawn
paintings.description: Mountain peaks catch the first light of dawn, glowing gold and amber above a sea of soft violet cloud. The sky overhead melts from deep indigo into warm rose — a moment of impossible colour that lasts only minutes before the ordinary day begins.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet sky gradients, dry brush for rock textures, lifted highlights on snow

paintings.title: Fighting Fish I
paintings.description: A teal Siamese fighting fish fans its elaborate fins against a deep dark background, white ink lines radiating outward like a signal or an aura — equal parts biological specimen and electric dream.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, wet-on-wet fish washes, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Fighting Fish II
paintings.description: A fire-red Betta splendens spreads its fins in full display, its crimson and orange plumage burning against the darkness. White ink lines radiate outward as if the fish itself is a source of heat and light.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, wet-on-wet fish washes, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Amber Falls
paintings.description: A wide waterfall crashes through an autumnal canopy of lime-green and golden-yellow foliage. Birds cut across the pale sky above the mist. The warm and cool tones push against each other — the forest alive with the particular energy of a season in transition.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet canopy washes, negative painting for birds, dry brush waterfall, lifted mist highlights

paintings.title: Jungle Plunge
paintings.description: A tall jungle waterfall drops straight through a cathedral of dense green rainforest. Birds wade at the shallow base. The foliage presses in from every side — abundant, layered, alive — the water the only vertical break in all that growth.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet layered foliage, controlled dry brush for the water column, negative painting for birds

paintings.title: Robin on a Post
paintings.description: A European robin perches on a weathered post, tilting its head to the right with an alert, watchful expression. The background is a loose, freely painted wash of blue-green and ochre — unfussy and immediate, all attention on the bird.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet background, controlled wet-on-dry for bird plumage, ink detail for eye and beak

paintings.title: The Spine
paintings.description: A dramatic ridge of snow-dusted peaks cuts across the composition like a spine. Deep blue shadows fill the crevices; bright sunlight catches the high edges. The sky behind is washed clean and cold — altitude, silence, scale.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet sky wash, dry brush for rock texture, masking fluid for snow highlights

paintings.title: Ganesha II
paintings.description: Lord Ganesha rendered in celestial blue, his crown and robes worked in warm gold against a dark, smoky background. The blue skin — a mark of divinity — gives this Ganesha a quality at once grounded and otherworldly. Painted with reverence and precision.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet dark background, layered wet-on-dry for figure detail, gold ink highlights

paintings.title: The Colony
paintings.description: A group of superb fairy-wrens clusters on a branch — one cobalt male blazing among the browns and greys of females and juveniles. White ink lines stream across the dark background like falling rain or static discharge, giving the scene an electric, charged quality.
paintings.technique: Dark wet-on-wet background, detailed dry-brush bird work, white gel pen rain-line overlay

paintings.title: The Gorge
paintings.description: A deep canyon drops away to reveal a river threading through a lush green valley floor far below. Sheer walls rise on either side, their dark stone faces streaked with mineral colour. The scale is vertiginous — the kind of place that makes you feel the deep time of the earth.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet foliage and river, dry brush for rock faces, negative painting for canyon depth

paintings.title: Sacred Lotus
paintings.description: A red lotus floats in darkness, its petals precisely detailed, white ink lines radiating outward from the bloom like light from a spiritual source. The lotus as symbol — purity rising from murk — rendered in deep pigment and fine line.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, layered wet-on-dry petal work, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Betta Vortex
paintings.description: Two Betta fish — one fire-orange, one deep violet — spiral around each other in a dark vortex. Their fins trail through the water in long, silk-like ribbons. The composition hovers between fight and dance; it's impossible to tell which it is.
paintings.technique: Dark wet-on-wet background, swirl blending for vortex, layered fish detail, white gel pen highlights

paintings.title: Macaw in Flight
paintings.description: A blue-and-gold macaw spreads its wings in full flight against a dark background, its vivid yellow underside and cobalt blue back caught mid-stroke. White ink lines radiate outward — the bird at the centre of its own force field.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, detailed wet-on-dry feather layering, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Cat in the Garden
paintings.description: A black-and-white cat peers through a screen of green foliage, its pale face and wide eyes emerging from the leaves. The watercolour has a softness that the cat's direct gaze immediately cuts through — cool, composed, a little unsettling.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet foliage, controlled dry-brush for cat fur detail, ink linework for face and eyes

paintings.title: Bumblebee
paintings.description: A bumblebee hangs in the air against a soft lavender background, its fuzzy body a study in black and amber. Honeycomb patterns float in the upper corners in white ink — a nod to the unseen architecture of the hive the bee is always returning to.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet lavender background, detailed dry-brush fur texture, white gel pen honeycomb overlay

paintings.title: Robin in the Garden
paintings.description: A European robin stands front-on, plump and alert, its orange-red breast vivid against a freely painted wash of green and teal. The brush marks are loose and visible — less illustration, more impression of a bird caught in a moment of stillness.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet background, wet-on-dry breast layering, ink linework for eye and beak detail

paintings.title: Valley of the Spire
paintings.description: A lone rocky pinnacle rises above a sweeping green valley floor, the landscape around it vivid with summer colour — bright meadows, a winding river, a small waterfall spilling over a dark ledge in the foreground. The scale is epic; the light is clear and direct.
paintings.technique: Bold wet-on-wet sky and mountain washes, dry brush for rock and meadow detail, controlled waterfall rendering

paintings.title: Robin in the Rain
paintings.description: A European robin perches on a bare branch in the rain, its orange breast glowing against a cold blue-grey background. White ink lines streak diagonally across the composition — the rain made visible, the bird holding its ground in the middle of it.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet dark background, detailed bird layering, white gel pen rain-line overlay

paintings.title: Dance in the Rain
paintings.description: A woman in a flowing coral-red dress spins alone in the rain, her arms outstretched, dress billowing. The background is deep violet — storm colour — and white ink lines streak down like rain caught mid-fall. Joy and abandon in the middle of a downpour.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet violet background, loose figure rendering, white gel pen rain-line overlay, lifted reflections in puddle

paintings.title: Highland Cascade
paintings.description: A river winds across a wide highland plateau before dropping over a dark ledge as a bright waterfall. Beyond, green hills rise in gentle ridges against an open blue sky with drifting cloud. The light is generous; the landscape is open and unhurried.
paintings.technique: Bold wet-on-wet sky and hill washes, dry brush for plateau and rock texture, controlled waterfall rendering
